notes:
POC focus: evaluate hosted embeddings -> see hit to query latency and cost -> then trial Dedicated for nightly bulk runs and predictable throughput.

Key technical requirements / excerpts from calls:
- Workload: semantic search for product help center + support agent reranking. Nightly batch reindex of ~300k new/updated docs; live queries: peak ~200 qps, typical 30-60 qps.
- Targets: user-facing search P95 <= 150ms end-to-end (query + vector DB + rerank). Batch embedding window: finish within 6 hours overnight.
- Integration: current stack uses Elastic kNN + Redis for ephemeral state. Preferred flow: S3 -> Redwood hosted embeddings -> write vectors to Pinecone (or PGVector) via worker. Want minimal infra changes.
- Embedding model preferences: 1536-d embeddings or equivalently high-quality open embeddings. Want the ability to test different embedding sizes for cost/perf.
- Throughput: need bulk embedding throughput ~200k docs/day; single-document embedding latency < 60ms for interactive tooling.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate. CTO: "we can trade off latency for cost on batch jobs, but not on live queries." Wants clear cost model for Hosted vs Dedicated.
- Security/compliance: must support SSO (SAML), audit logs for inference calls, KMS for keys, and US data residency for production indices. Security team requested Redwood security FAQ and SOC2 evidence (Drive link).
- Operational concerns: automatic reconnects/retries for vector writes, backpressure in worker when Pinecone rate-limited, and idempotency for bulk jobs.
- POC results so far: relevance better than Elastic baseline on manual eval set, but tail latency occasionally spikes due to current vector DB config. SE proposed Dedicated with reserved slots for consistent kernel selection and reduced variance.

Quotes / call snippets:
- CTO (Anya Hsu): "If we can hit P95 <150ms and not blow the budget on nightly indexing, this is a go."
- Head of ML (Rafael): "We need predictable throughput for re-index jobs — spikes kill our other infra."
